claims.summary: Naro et al. describe a gente and nós as first-person plural pronouns in Brazilian Portuguese; the cited standard pattern pairs nós with -mos and prefers third-person singular agreement with a gente.
Naro et al. report popular-speech variants nós fala and a gente falamos, so third-person singular is not presented as invariant across the speech data.
Zilles compares Southern Brazilian data from the 1970s and 1990s and describes the development of a gente as a pronoun increasingly replacing nós in speech in the studied region.
The four cited forms nós falamos, a gente fala, nós fala, and a gente falamos are explicitly mentioned by Naro et al.
